home.tagline: Your free online music laboratory: high-precision chord recognition, 6-stem audio splitter, and interactive guitar tools.
home.html:
What is Guitariz Studio?

Guitariz Studio is a free, browser-based music toolkit built for guitarists, songwriters, producers, and music students who want professional-grade audio analysis without a subscription. Instead of paying for desktop software or juggling five different apps, you get chord recognition, stem separation, and an interactive scale explorer in one place — all running through your browser.

The project started as an open-source effort by Abhinav Vaidya to make the kind of tools usually locked behind paywalls (chord detection engines, source separation models, scale visualizers) freely accessible to anyone learning or working with music. It's still open-source today, with an active contributor community shipping new features.

Who uses Guitariz

  • Songwriters figuring out the chords behind a reference track
  • Guitar students learning scales, modes, and how they map to the fretboard
  • Producers who need clean vocal or instrumental stems without expensive plugins
  • Music theory learners exploring Western modes alongside Indian Raga structures — a comparison most tools don't offer

The tools

Chord AI — Upload an MP3 or paste a YouTube link and get chord progressions extracted automatically, powered by a custom-trained neural network.

Stem Splitter — Separate vocals, drums, bass, and other instruments from any track using Meta's Demucs source-separation model.

Scale Explorer — An interactive fretboard that maps out major, minor, pentatonic, modal, and Raga-based scale patterns in real time.

Why it's free

Guitariz doesn't charge for its core tools because the goal is access, not gatekeeping. The project is supported through optional ads and a lightweight premium tier for advanced processing — the core chord detection, scale tools, and basic stem separation stay free for everyone.

chordAi.title: Chord AI Free - Audio to Chord Recognition AI | Guitariz
chordAi.description: Extract chords, tempo, and scales from any song for free with Chord AI. Advanced AI chord recognition and harmonic transcription with no subscription.
chordAi.tagline: Neural audio chord detection and harmonic transcription. Extract guitar chords and keys automatically from MP3s or YouTube.
chordAi.html:
How Chord AI works

Most free "chord detector" tools online use basic pitch-class profiling and guess wrong on anything beyond simple major/minor triads. Chord AI takes a more deliberate DSP-based approach built on Librosa's audio analysis pipeline: harmonic-percussive source separation (HPSS) isolates the tonal content from percussive noise, chroma features are extracted from the cleaned signal, and those features are matched against chord templates to identify the most likely chord at each point in the track.

Post-processing. Raw frame-by-frame chord guesses are smoothed using a Viterbi-based Hidden Markov Model in log-space, which enforces musically plausible chord transitions instead of letting the output flip between chords every fraction of a second. This is the difference between an unreadable chord chart and one you can actually play along with.

From MP3 or YouTube. You can either upload an audio file directly or paste a YouTube link — Guitariz handles extraction and analysis in the background.

What's next. A neural network-based recognition model (CRNN, trained to significantly outperform the current DSP baseline) is in active development and will roll out as an additional "Accurate mode" alongside the current detection engine — built to run efficiently in-browser and on the server via ONNX Runtime once released.

What you get

  • A full chord progression timeline for the track
  • Detected key signature
  • Tempo (BPM)
  • Chord symbols in standard notation (maj, min, 7, maj7, sus, dim, etc.)

stemSeparator.title: Stem Splitter AI - Free 6-Stem Audio Extractor | Guitariz
stemSeparator.description: Separate any song into 6 stems with Stem Splitter AI: vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, and other. High-quality AI stem extraction for music production.
stemSeparator.tagline: AI-powered 6-stem track separation. Isolate vocals, drums, bass, guitar, and piano from any track using Meta's Demucs.
stemSeparator.html:
How stem separation works

Stem separation splits a finished mix back into its individual parts — vocals, drums, bass, and "other" (everything else: guitars, synths, strings). Guitariz's stem splitter runs on Demucs, Meta AI's open-source source separation model, which uses a deep neural network trained on isolated multitrack recordings to learn what a vocal, a kick drum, or a bassline sounds like in isolation — even when they're layered on top of each other in a finished mix.

What it's useful for

  • Producers isolating a vocal for sampling, remixing, or mashups
  • Singers creating instrumental backing tracks from a reference song
  • Musicians removing vocals to practice playing along
  • Transcribers isolating bass or drums to work out a part in detail

What you get

Four separated stems from any uploaded track: vocals, drums, bass, and other instruments — each downloadable individually.

scales.title: Guitar Scale Explorer - Scale Patterns & Modes | Guitariz
scales.description: Explore guitar scales and modes visually. Map Western modes and Indian Classical music Ragas (Bhairav, Yaman, Bilawal) onto an interactive guitar neck.
scales.tagline: Interactive guitar neck and keyboard. Visualize Western modes and Indian Classical Ragas across the fretboard dynamically.
scales.html:
Interactive Scale & Mode Explorer

The Scale Explorer maps guitar scales and modes directly onto an interactive fretboard, so you can see exactly where each note falls rather than memorizing shapes from a static diagram.

What's covered

  • Western scales and modes — major, natural/harmonic/melodic minor, pentatonic (major and minor), blues, and the full set of modal scales (Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Locrian, etc.)
  • Indian Ragas — a rare feature among guitar tools: explore Raga-based scale structures mapped onto standard guitar tuning, useful for players working across Western and Hindustani/Carnatic music traditions
  • Key and root selection — pick any root note and see the pattern transpose across the fretboard in real time

Why it matters for improvisation

Knowing a scale by name isn't the same as knowing where it lives on your instrument. Guitariz's fretboard view is built to close that gap — see the full pattern, identify the root notes at a glance, and internalize how a scale connects across positions instead of treating each shape as an isolated box.
